messages.subject: rmr v1.2 released
parts:
Please see the announcement. Main news is support for binary formats, with better support for R data types and the potential to read all sort of data from the Hadoop ecosystem, an efficiency-killing reduce bug solved and more. Please do not hesitate with comments and suggestions.


Antonio

On Saturday, March 3, 2012 2:49:42 PM UTC-8, Legacy wrote:

I am not yet familiar with rmr1.2. Could you provide a very basic example to start with because I am getting a lot of errors like below:
We wrote a tutorial for a reason. Should I paste it as an answer to this message or can you go and use the wiki?

> library(rmr)
>
> from.dfs(mapreduce(to.dfs(1:100),input.format="native",backend.parameters=list("hadoop")))
Don't use backend.parameters until you absolutely know what you are doing. This commands is incorrect and its goals unclear to me.

Warning: $HADOOP_HOME is deprecated.

12/03/03 23:46:47 ERROR streaming.StreamJob: Missing required options: input, output
Usage: $HADOOP_HOME/bin/hadoop jar \
          $HADOOP_HOME/hadoop-streaming.jar [options]
Options:
  -input    <path>     DFS input file(s) for the Map step
  -output   <path>     DFS output directory for the Reduce step
  -mapper   <cmd|JavaClassName>      The streaming command to run
  -combiner <cmd|JavaClassName> The streaming command to run
  -reducer  <cmd|JavaClassName>      The streaming command to run
  -file     <file>     File/dir to be shipped in the Job jar file
  -inputformat TextInputFormat(default)|SequenceFileAsTextInputFormat|JavaClassName Optional.
  -outputformat TextOutputFormat(default)|JavaClassName  Optional.

  -numReduceTasks <num>  Optional.
  -inputreader <spec>  Optional.
  -cmdenv   <n>=<v>    Optional. Pass env.var to streaming commands
  -mapdebug <path>  Optional. To run this script when a map task fails
  -reducedebug <path>  Optional. To run this script when a reduce task fails
  -verbose

Generic options supported are
-conf <configuration file>     specify an application configuration file
-D <property=value>            use value for given property
-fs <local|namenode:port>      specify a namenode
-jt <local|jobtracker:port>    specify a job tracker
-files <comma separated list of files>    specify comma separated files to be copied to the map reduce cluster
-libjars <comma separated list of jars>    specify comma separated jar files to include in the classpath.
-archives <comma separated list of archives>    specify comma separated archives to be unarchived on the compute machines.

The general command line syntax is
bin/hadoop command [genericOptions] [commandOptions]


For more details about these options:
Use $HADOOP_HOME/bin/hadoop jar build/hadoop-streaming.jar -info

Streaming Job Failed!
Warning: $HADOOP_HOME is deprecated.

-inputformat : class not found : org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat
Streaming Job Failed!
Error in mr(map = map, reduce = reduce, reduce.on.data.frame = reduce.on.data.frame,  :
  hadoop streaming failed with error code 1

Of course with backend.parameters you get a lot of rope and you can mess up the streaming command. That's why it's an advanced argument and I gave plenty of warning that it breaks the abstraction and you should use it only if absolutely necessary. If you are still learning rmr, just don't touch it, ever. There is no valid  reason to do otherwise. The thing will blow up in your face. I told you so. Start from the Tutorial. Moreover your version of hadoop doesn't have a crucial patch (HADOOP-1722). Use CDH3 if you want to make your life simple.


Antonio

On Sunday, 4 March 2012 17:44:15 UTC+1, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
Two things, first you are more likely to find qualified hadoop help on forums other than this one. Second, just looking at the pasted log, there is nothing particularly bad there. Those are INFO messages, whatever they mean. there is no error. Maybe it shuts itself down after completing a format? Have you tried starting all the daemons as per Cloudera documentation and then scour all the logs for an ERROR? Another simpler alternative is to use standalone mode while you are learning so that you don't have to deal with daemons, ports and what not. Of course you are not going to do big data in standalone. I always start in standalone because I can see stderr of R directly in console. I can't program without that and then I push a program to the cluster and finish it there, but that's just my workflow. I hope this helps


Antonio

Don't use backend.parameters until you absolutely know what you are doing. This commands is incorrect and its goals unclear to me.

Of course with backend.parameters you get a lot of rope and you can mess up the streaming command. That's why it's an advanced argument and I gave plenty of warning that it breaks the abstraction and you should use it only if absolutely necessary. If you are still learning rmr, just don't touch it, ever. There is no valid  reason to do otherwise. The thing will blow up in your face. I told you so. Start from the Tutorial. Moreover your version of hadoop doesn't have a crucial patch (HADOOP-1722). Use CDH3 if you want to make your life simple.


Antonio
